title: Stop swaddling once a baby starts to roll, which NICHD says is usually around three months
summary: NICHD's Safe to Sleep FAQ says to avoid swaddling once a baby starts to roll, usually around three months, because a swaddled baby can have trouble moving off the stomach.
body: The FAQ says to avoid swaddling once the baby starts to roll over, and it puts that change at usually around 3 months of age. Back sleeping for a swaddled baby matters, it says, because the baby may have trouble moving out of a stomach or side position while swaddled, which raises the risk of suffocation and other sleep-related deaths. The page also says stomach sleeping carries the highest risk of SIDS, and that the risk is very high for a baby who usually sleeps on the back but is placed on the stomach, and for a baby who is swaddled and rolls onto the stomach. Usually around three months is the page's timing, not a rule that every baby rolls on that day. If a baby rolls earlier or later, the trigger the page names is the rolling, not the birthday.

sources.title: Safe to Sleep: Frequently Asked Questions
